public_rationale: The shortage component is supported by UK census findings and reporting from US academic departments. The worldwide claim that not one radiologist had been replaced is not established by those shortages. North Denmark documented AI taking over some reading work, while reallocating doctors to other duties; that does not establish job displacement. No verified pre-post displacement case was found, but absence of a found case cannot prove zero. The combined claim therefore remains unresolved.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading replacement as job displacement rather than substitution on individual tasks.
Public staffing records may omit individual displacements or their causes.
The cited shortage findings have different reporting dates and geographic coverage.
The global zero-replacement outcome was not publicly established in the records found by the evaluation date.

our_interpretation: The retrospective replacement assertion covers the period from Hinton's stated 2016 prediction through the post on 2025-03-02. The year-level reference is represented by a start date of 2016-01-01.

In the discussion of whether to train radiologists, replacement ordinarily means an occupied radiologist position displaced because AI takes over the role. Automating tasks while retaining the radiologist for other work does not establish that.

The shortage assertion concerns conditions near publication. I use the latest workforce reporting publicly available before the post, while retaining the broader retrospective target period required by the replacement assertion.
Many parts of the world means shortages across multiple countries or regions, rather than every country.
'My understanding is' qualifies confidence; it does not create a conditional antecedent or remove the factual assertion.
The startup count is contextual framing, rather than a separately specified population or measure of replacement.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable evidence establishes no AI-caused displacement of a radiologist position during the retrospective period, and workforce evidence establishes shortages across multiple countries or regions near publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one documented occupied radiologist position was displaced by AI by 2025-03-02, or sufficiently broad workforce evidence refutes the assertion of geographically widespread shortages. Task automation alone does not contradict the job-displacement reading.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A verified staffing record showing one radiologist position displaced by AI by March 2, 2025 would contradict the zero assertion. Supporting it requires sufficiently comprehensive retrospective employment evidence, beyond shortages and the absence of reported cases.
